title: Convergence to collusion in algorithmic pricing
abstract: arXiv:2604.15825v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Artificial intelligence algorithms are increasingly used by firms to set prices. Previous research shows that they can learn to collude, but how quickly and reliably they can do so has remained an open question. I study average-reward soft actor-critic algorithms that set continuous prices in the workhorse environment of this literature: a repeated Bertrand duopoly with symmetric firms, deterministic logit demand, and constant marginal costs, where agents observe only market prices and their own profits. The algorithms can converge to a collusive outcome within 50,000 periods, and in 36% of simulations learned punishments make one-period deviations unprofitable, so that high prices are mutual best responses. Successful simulations show cooperative behaviour supported by reward-punishment schemes that discourage deviations. translated_title: 算法定价中向合谋的收敛
translated_abstract: 人工智能算法正被企业越来越多地用于定价。以往的研究表明，这些算法能够学会合谋，但它们能以多快的速度、多高的可靠性做到这一点仍是一个悬而未决的问题。我研究了在该文献的标准环境中设定连续价格的平均奖励软演员-评论家（soft actor-critic）算法：一个具有对称企业、确定性logit需求和恒定边际成本的重复伯特兰双寡头模型，其中智能体只能观察到市场价格和自身利润。这些算法可以在50,000个周期内收敛到合谋结果，并且在36%的模拟中，学习到的惩罚机制使得单期偏离无利可图，从而使高价成为相互的最优反应。成功的模拟显示了由抑制偏离的奖励-惩罚方案所支撑的合作行为。当高价缺乏惩罚机制支撑时，有利可图的偏离通常只有百分之一的量级。
tldr: 该论文首次量化了平均奖励软演员-评论家算法在重复伯特兰双寡头环境中向合谋收敛的速度与可靠性，发现算法可在5万个周期内收敛至合谋结果，并在36%的模拟中通过学习到的惩罚机制使高价成为相互最优反应。
en_tdlr: This paper quantifies how quickly and reliably average-reward soft actor-critic algorithms converge to collusion in a repeated Bertrand duopoly, showing convergence within 50,000 periods and punishment-supported collusive prices in 36% of simulations.
